@copilot Simplify this PR's Akka HTTP regression test and establish the supported real-world trigger for dispatcher callback rejection.

The user originally requested integration coverage instead of mocks, but found the resulting 293-line ClientCallbackTest.scala excessively complicated and questioned whether the bug is an extreme edge case. The current test uses a real agent, ActorSystem, and HTTP server, but a custom RejectingDispatcher deliberately rejects execution-context callbacks while actor mailbox processing continues. This proves the injected failure mechanism, not that a normal overloaded or shutting-down dispatcher reaches it.

Investigate the concrete Akka dispatcher/executor implementations and dependency versions supported by this module. Identify a supported configuration or lifecycle that can actually reject these instrumentation callbacks and explain the evidence. Do not assume ordinary default-dispatcher overload causes rejection. If a realistic trigger cannot be established, say so explicitly rather than presenting fault injection as a production reproduction.

Simplify instrumentation/akka/akka-http-10.0/javaagent/src/test/scala/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/akkahttp/v10_0/client/ClientCallbackTest.scala. Keep real agent-backed HTTP integration coverage, not mocks or direct advice invocation. Focus on a request pending when callback scheduling rejects, with the application-visible response completing and the client span ending despite rejection. Reuse existing module test fixtures where practical and remove redundant assertions already covered by the ordinary HTTP client tests. Keep relevant success/failure behavior protected without adding a large test matrix or flaky load/shutdown timing merely to simulate production.

Keep this scoped to PR #20694 and preserve its draft state and intended callback-rejection fix. Do not expand the production behavior based on speculation. Validate the smaller regression against baseline and latest dependencies and relevant semantic-convention modes, and confirm it detects the original hang when the callback fallback is absent. In your completion response, explain the verified trigger or remaining uncertainty and how the test was simplified. Update the PR description only if necessary to keep its claims accurate.

replies.body: Confirmed a supported lifecycle trigger, but not ordinary overload: Akka’s `Dispatcher.shutdown()` shuts down its executor, and `SaneRejectedExecutionHandler` throws `RejectedExecutionException` after shutdown; while active, it runs the rejected task inline. I verified this behavior in the minimum Akka Actor 2.4.14 and latest-tested 2.8.8. The test remains deterministic agent-backed fault injection, not a production shutdown-timing reproduction. It now covers one pending real HTTP request, its completed response, and the ended client span; existing client tests retain normal success/error coverage. Commit: `7b70f68a`. The PR body’s regression bullet still describes the removed matrix; the accurate replacement is: “Verify a pending agent-backed HTTP response resolves and its client span ends after dispatcher callback rejection.” I could not edit the PR body with the available write tools.

@copilot Replace the integration regression in PR #20694 with the smaller, verified relative-URI failure reproduction. The user asked whether ClientCallbackTest.scala could be simpler and then invoked /cloud to have you make that change. Keep this scoped to the existing PR and preserve its draft state and production fix.

Change instrumentation/akka/akka-http-10.0/javaagent/src/test/scala/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/akkahttp/v10_0/client/ClientCallbackTest.scala to make a real Http.singleRequest call with a relative URI after saturating Akka's stock affinity executor. Akka returns an already-failed future with IllegalUriException for this input, without network I/O. This reproduces the same dropped instrumentation callback and replacement-future hang without an HTTP server or response coordination. Replace the current network regression rather than adding a second test or fixture. Remove the Armeria server, request-received/server-response futures, response-body assertions, and separate HTTP stream dispatcher.

Use the existing real ActorSystem and installed AgentInstrumentationExtension. Configure akka.actor.default-dispatcher.executor = "affinity-pool-executor", with affinity-pool-executor.parallelism-min = 1, parallelism-max = 1, and task-queue-size = 64. Set akka.loggers-dispatcher = "akka.actor.default-blocking-io-dispatcher" so rejection reporting remains operational. Initialize ActorMaterializer and Http.get(system) before filling the queue. Block the worker with the existing latch pattern and submit ordinary no-op tasks until the stock executor actually throws RejectedExecutionException. Do not introduce mocks, a custom rejecting dispatcher, manually thrown rejection exceptions, artificial delays, or direct advice/helper invocation. Keep reliable resource cleanup and release the worker in finally before ActorSystem termination. Keep the PER_CLASS lifecycle and latest-dependency assumption; baseline Akka 2.4 does not provide the affinity executor.

The core assertion is val failure = Await.result(http.singleRequest(HttpRequest(uri = "/relative")).failed, 5.seconds), followed by an assertion that failure is IllegalUriException. Assert the complete exported trace with one GET CLIENT span, error status, and the original exception. A temporary 107-line agent-backed probe using this exact setup has already been verified locally against Akka HTTP 10.5.3 and Actor/Stream 2.8.8: it passes with the fallback; changing only the advice execution context from new CallbackExecutionContext(actorSystem.dispatcher()) to actorSystem.dispatcher() makes the same call time out after five seconds. Restoring the fix passes again. Use this established recipe rather than investigating shutdown or inventing a new trigger. Keep all production changes as they currently stand.

Validate the smaller regression under latest dependencies in the normal and preview-semconv tasks, verify it intentionally skips against baseline dependencies, and keep the existing ordinary client tests passing. Confirm the negative control detects the original hang and restore production code exactly afterward. The earlier real-server experiment already established that a successful network response can also remain pending after all 64 queued tasks drain; that is supporting investigation evidence, not a requirement to retain that larger test.

Update only stale PR-description claims so readers can distinguish the new committed relative-URI failure regression from the earlier successful-response investigation. In particular, do not keep saying the committed regression runs an HTTP server, and do not imply ordinary default-fork-join overload or normal shutdown has been demonstrated. Preserve the template comment and keep the description concise. Do not request another review or create an unrelated PR. Report the delivered commit and the validation/negative-control outcome when finished.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly with the simpler fix selected by the user: always execute the agent's HTTP client completion callbacks inline, and include the equivalent Pekko HTTP fix in this same PR. Keep its existing source branch and draft state. The separate large redesign PR #20960 has been closed; do not use that redesign or create another PR.

The two agent-installed completion callbacks end the client span and complete the existing replacement promise under the captured parent context. Currently Akka's CallbackExecutionContext first submits them to the actor-system dispatcher and falls back to runnable.run() only after RejectedExecutionException. Replace that policy with a small direct execution context that always runs these agent callbacks on the submitting thread. Wire both callbacks to it in Akka HTTP and Pekko HTTP. Retain the existing FutureWrapper promise-based context propagation. Do not add Scala promise instrumentation, future markers, registries, combinator wrapping, or independent instrumentation modules. Application callbacks must continue to use the execution contexts selected by the application; do not wrap those execution contexts with a rejection fallback or force asynchronous application callbacks inline. Preserve the original HTTP result or failure and existing telemetry identities. Remove dispatcher access or reflection helpers only where this change makes them obsolete. Keep callback failure reporting explicit using repository-standard instrumentation logging, and preserve compatibility with Scala 2.11's ExecutionContext.prepare contract.

Relevant production code is under instrumentation/akka/akka-http-10.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/akkahttp/v10_0/client and instrumentation/pekko/pekko-http-1.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/pekkohttp/v1_0/client. Both HttpExtClientInstrumentation classes register OnCompleteHandler and call FutureWrapper.wrap with an actor dispatcher. This dispatcher dependency is the cause of the agent-created replacement future remaining pending after callback rejection.

Keep the regression focused and installed-agent-backed. Preserve the real affinity-queue saturation reproduction in Akka's ClientCallbackTest and add equivalent Pekko coverage. Also exercise a blocked but accepting single-worker dispatcher with an immediate relative-URI request failure, so the regression proves the callbacks are always inline rather than merely falling back after rejection. Initialize the real ActorSystem, materializer, and Http extension before blocking the dispatcher. Assert the application-visible future is completed and the client span ends while the dispatcher cannot run callbacks; verify the original IllegalUriException. Release blocked workers in finally and terminate owned systems reliably. No mocks, custom rejecting dispatchers, directly invoked advice/helpers, or timing-based shutdown tests. Akka's baseline 2.4 has no affinity executor and also has no predefined akka.actor.default-blocking-io-dispatcher; use a logger configuration that exists in every tested version. Retain the latest-only assumption only for Akka's affinity case, not the blocked-but-accepting regression. Keep the tests small and reuse existing ordinary client callback coverage instead of adding a broad new matrix.

Run the relevant formatting and focused installed-agent regressions, including ordinary successful callbacks with and without a parent and the error callback, against baseline and latest dependencies for both modules. Exercise the existing Pekko Scala 3 suite where feasible, without changing unrelated build defaults. If the cloud host lacks the default test JDK, the repository supports -PtestJavaVersion=25. Confirm the accepting-but-blocked regression detects the prior dispatcher-based implementation, then restore the inline fix. Report delivered commits, the tests actually run and their results, and any genuine validation limitation.

threads.body: [Javaagent] The description promises inline execution only after dispatcher rejection, with rejection reported through the original execution context, but both Akka and Pekko now run every instrumentation callback inline and report callback failures through JUL. This also changes callback threading for healthy requests; the same change appears in Pekko's `HttpExtClientInstrumentation.java:88–90`. Either implement the documented dispatcher-delegating fallback or update the description to explain and justify unconditional inline execution and the changed failure reporting for both libraries.

replies.body: Updated the title and description to match the chosen behavior for both Akka and Pekko. Unconditional inline execution is intentional: the agent no longer submits span completion or promise forwarding to the actor dispatcher, so neither callback can be stranded by its queue. The existing promise-based context propagation and application-selected callback execution contexts remain. Unexpected instrumentation callback failures are logged through JUL; there is no dispatcher submission rejection to report.

threads.body: [Javaagent] Make both this class and `INSTANCE` public because `SingleRequestAdvice.methodExit` references them directly. When the injecting transformer inlines that advice into `HttpExt`, these package-private accesses fail with `IllegalAccessError`, preventing completion-handler registration. This violates the direct-advice visibility rule in `.github/instructions/java-style.instructions.md:13–15`, which applies even with `inline = false`; the constructor can remain private.

replies.body: Fixed in 500c597f. Pekko's DirectExecutionContext and INSTANCE are now public so advice inlined into HttpExt can access them; the constructor remains private. Akka's helper stays package-private because it is accessed transitively from the same-package AdviceScope.end helper.

@copilot Fix the remaining in-scope visibility defect on this existing PR without changing the chosen always-inline behavior or expanding the implementation.

Latest-head review 5646535410 correctly identified that Pekko's new DirectExecutionContext and its INSTANCE field are package-private even though SingleRequestAdvice.methodExit references them directly. This is not disproved by inline = false on the source advice. The injecting TypeTransformerImpl explicitly applies new AdviceInliningPoolStrategy(poolStrategy, true), which rewrites the annotation to inline the advice into org.apache.pekko.http.scaladsl.HttpExt. Accessing the package-private helper from that class then causes IllegalAccessError and skips completion-handler registration. The current repository's .github/instructions/java-style.instructions.md also explicitly requires public visibility for direct advice references.

Make instrumentation/pekko/pekko-http-1.0/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/pekkohttp/v1_0/client/DirectExecutionContext.java and its INSTANCE field public, retaining the private constructor and final class. Akka's equivalent helper is accessed transitively from AdviceScope.end in the same package, so do not broaden its visibility without another concrete need. Keep both clients' completion callbacks always inline, preserve FutureWrapper context propagation and application-selected callback execution contexts, and leave the implementation otherwise unchanged.

Validate the focused Pekko installed-agent regressions and ordinary success/parent/no-parent/error callbacks. Exercise the injecting transformation path if the repository provides a supported test mode for it, as well as the normal mode; use the repository's existing switches instead of inventing configuration or changing defaults. Run relevant formatting and report the actual commands and outcomes, including any unavailable test mode. The default test JDK can be overridden with -PtestJavaVersion=25 if necessary. Update this same draft PR directly.
